questions.q: Three metal rods of the same material and identical in all respects are joined as shown in the figure. The temperatures at the ends of these rods are maintained as indicated. Assuming no heat energy loss occurs through the curved surfaces of the rods, the temperature at the junction x is [figure: one rod at 0°C meets junction X, two other identical rods from X go to two ends both at 90°C]
questions.explanation: Heat balance at the junction with identical rods gives $T_x-0=2(90-T_x)$, so $3T_x=180$ and $T_x=60\,{}^\circ C$.

questions.q: A solid cube of mass m at a temperature $\theta_0$ is heated at a constant rate. It becomes liquid at temperature $\theta_1$ and vapour at temperature $\theta_2$. Let $s_1$ and $s_2$ be specific heats in its solid and liquid states respectively. If $L_f$ and $L_v$ are latent heats of fusion and vaporisation respectively, then the minimum heat energy supplied to the cube until it vaporises is
questions.explanation: Total heat = heating the solid + melting + heating the liquid + vaporising: $Q=ms_1(\theta_1-\theta_0)+mL_f+ms_2(\theta_2-\theta_1)+mL_v$.

questions.q: 100 g of ice at 0 °C is mixed with 100 g of water at 100 °C. The final temperature of the mixture is [Take L$_f$ = 3.36 × 10$^5$ J kg$^{-1}$ and S$_w$ = 4.2 × 10$^3$ J kg$^{-1}$k$^{-1}$]

Which of the following curves represent the variation of coefficient of volume expansion of an ideal gas at constant pressure? (A) $\alpha_v$ vs T: straight line through the origin, positive slope. (B) $\alpha_v$ vs 1/T: straight line through the origin, positive slope. (C) $\alpha_v$ vs 1/T: horizontal straight line. (D) $\alpha_v$ vs T: straight line with negative slope.
questions.explanation: For an ideal gas at constant pressure, $V\propto T$ so $\alpha_v=\dfrac{1}{V}\dfrac{dV}{dT}=\dfrac{1}{T}$, which is a straight line through the origin when plotted against $1/T$.

questions.q: A cup of tea cools from 65.5°C to 62.5°C in 1 minute in a room at 22.5°C. How long will it take to cool from 46.5°C to 40.5°C in the same room?
questions.explanation: By Newton's law of cooling, (θ$_1$−θ$_2$)/t = k(θ$_{avg}$−θ$_0$). First case: 3/1 = k(64−22.5) ⟹ k = 3/41.5. Second case: 6/t = k(43.5−22.5) = k(21) ⟹ t = 6/(21×3/41.5) ≈ 4 minutes.

questions.q: The S.I. unit of specific heat capacity is
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity is heat required per unit mass per unit temperature rise, with SI unit J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A pan filled with hot food cools from 94°C to 86°C in 2 minutes. When the room temperature is 20°C. How long will it cool from 74°C to 66°C?
questions.explanation: By Newton's law of cooling, $\dfrac{\Delta T}{t}=k\left(T_{avg}-T_0\right)$. First case: $4/2=k(90-20)\Rightarrow k=1/35$. Second case: $8/t=\dfrac{1}{35}(70-20)\Rightarrow t=8\times35/50=2.8$ minutes.

questions.q: Four rods with different radii r and length l are used to connect two heat reservoirs at different temperature. Which one will conduct most heat?
questions.explanation: Heat conducted $\propto \dfrac{r^2}{l}$. Computing $r^2/l$ for each: 1, 2, 2, 8. Option (4) gives the largest value, so it conducts most heat.

questions.q: Water is heated from 0 °C to 10 °C, then its volume
questions.explanation: Water shows anomalous expansion: its volume decreases from 0°C to 4°C (density is maximum at 4°C) and then increases from 4°C to 10°C.

questions.q: 1 gram of ice is mixed with 1 gram of steam. At thermal equilibrium, the temperature of the mixture is
questions.explanation: Heat released by 1 g of steam condensing (540 cal) far exceeds the heat needed to melt the ice and raise it to 100°C (80+100=180 cal), so the equilibrium temperature is 100°C, with some steam left uncondensed.

questions.q: In anomalous expansion of water, at what temperature, the density of water is maximum?
questions.explanation: Water has its maximum density at 4 $^{\circ}$C due to anomalous expansion.

questions.q: A solid cylinder of radius R made of a material of thermal conductivity K$_1$ is surrounded by a cylindrical shell of inner radius R and outer radius 2R made of a material of thermal conductivity K$_2$. The two ends of the combined system are maintained at two different temperatures. Then there is no loss of heat across the cylindrical surface and the system is in steady state. The effective thermal conductivity of the system is
questions.explanation: The core and shell conduct heat in parallel (same length, no radial loss); their cross-sectional areas are $\pi R^2$ and $3\pi R^2$, so $K_{eff}=\dfrac{K_1(\pi R^2)+K_2(3\pi R^2)}{4\pi R^2}=\dfrac{K_1+3K_2}{4}$.

questions.q: Two stars A and B radiate maximum energy at the wavelengths of 360 nm and 480 nm respectively. Then the ratio of the surface temperatures of A and B is
questions.explanation: By Wien's displacement law, $T\propto1/\lambda_{max}$, so $T_A:T_B=\lambda_B:\lambda_A=480:360=4:3$.

questions.q: A, B and C are three identical conductors but made of different materials, kept in contact in a line [figure: rod A-B-C joined end to end; free end of A at 100°C, free end of C at 0°C]. Their thermal conductivities are K, 2K and K/2. The free end of A is at 100°C and the free end of C is at 0°C. During steady state, the temperature of the junction of A and B is nearly ..... °C.
questions.explanation: In series conduction the heat current is the same through each rod; solving K(100-T$_1$) = 2K(T$_1$-T$_2$) = (K/2)T$_2$ for the A-B junction gives T$_1$ = 500/7 $\approx$ 71°C.

questions.q: A hot body is allowed to cool. The surrounding temperature is constant at 30 °C. The body takes time t$_1$ to cool from 90 °C to 89 °C and time t$_2$ to cool from 60 °C to 59.5 °C. Then,
questions.explanation: By Newton's law of cooling, $\dfrac{\Delta\theta}{t}=k(\theta_{avg}-\theta_0)$; the first case gives $1/t_1=k(59.5)$ and the second gives $0.5/t_2=k(29.75)$, both equal to $59.5k$, so $t_1=t_2$.

questions.q: Three identical rods $A$, $B$ and $C$ are placed end to end. A temperature difference is maintained between the free ends of $A$ and $C$. The thermal conductivity of $B$ is THRICE that of $C$ and HALF of that of $A$. The effective thermal conductivity of the system will be ........................ ($K_A$ is the thermal conductivity of rod $A$).
questions.explanation: With $K_A=6k$, $K_B=3k$, $K_C=k$, for identical rods in series: $3/K_{eff}=1/K_A+1/K_B+1/K_C = 3/(2k)$, giving $K_{eff}=2k=\dfrac{1}{3}K_A$.

questions.q: The quantities of heat required to raise the temperatures of two copper spheres of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ ($r_1 = 1.5 r_2$) through 1 K are in the ratio of .................
questions.explanation: Heat required $Q=mc\Delta T \propto r^3$ (same material), so $Q_1/Q_2=(r_1/r_2)^3=(1.5)^3=27/8$.

questions.q:
Which one of the following is $
u_m - T$ graph for perfectly black body? $
u_m$ is the frequency of radiation with maximum intensity. $T$ is the absolute temperature. [Graph of $
u_m$ (Hz) versus $T$ (K) shows four curves: A rises steeply then flattens; B rises and flattens at a higher level further right; C rises roughly linearly starting from the origin; D is a horizontal constant line]
questions.explanation: By Wien's displacement law $\lambda_m T = \text{constant}$, so $\nu_m = c/\lambda_m \propto T$; the graph is a straight line through the origin, matching curve C.

questions.q: Two slabs are of the thicknesses $d_1$ and $d_2$. Their thermal conductivities are $K_1$ and $K_2$ respectively. They are in series. The free ends of the combination of these two slabs are kept at temperatures $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$. Assume $\theta_1 > \theta_2$. The temperature $\theta$ of their common junction is .....................
questions.explanation: Equating heat current through both slabs, $K_1A(\theta_1-\theta)/d_1=K_2A(\theta-\theta_2)/d_2$; solving gives $\theta=\dfrac{K_1\theta_1d_2+K_2\theta_2d_1}{K_1d_2+K_2d_1}$.

questions.q: Hot water cools from 60$^0$C to 50$^0$C in the first 10 minutes and to 42$^0$C in the next 10 minutes. Then the temperature of the surroundings is .....................
questions.explanation: Using Newton's law of cooling with average temperatures: $\dfrac{60-50}{10}=k(55-T_s)$ and $\dfrac{50-42}{10}=k(46-T_s)$; solving gives $T_s=10^\circ$C.

questions.q: $0.1\ \text{m}^3$ of water at 80 °C is mixed with $0.3\ \text{m}^3$ of water at 60 °C. The final temperature of the mixture is
questions.explanation: By conservation of heat (same liquid): $T=\dfrac{0.1\times80+0.3\times60}{0.4}=\dfrac{26}{0.4}=65\ \text{°C}$.

questions.q: Which of the following statement does not hold good for thermal radiation ?
options: The frequency changes when it travels from one medium to another.
The speed changes when it travels from one medium to another.
They travel in straight line in a given medium.
The wavelength changes when it travels from one medium to another.
questions.explanation: When radiation passes from one medium to another, its frequency remains unchanged; only its speed and wavelength change, so statement (1) is false and hence the correct choice.

questions.q: The amount of heat energy radiated by a metal at temperature 'T' is 'E'. When the temperature is increased to 3T, energy radiated is
questions.explanation: By Stefan's law $E\propto T^4$, so at $3T$ the energy becomes $3^4E=81E$.

questions.q: The surface temperature of the stars is determined using
questions.explanation: Wien's displacement law ($\lambda_m T = \text{constant}$) relates a star's peak emission wavelength to its surface temperature.
